title: Environment

competencies.title: Can sort household waste for recycling
Has kept a weather diary for 2 weeks
Can start and keep a compost bin
Can run a local nature survey
Can carry out a home energy audit
Can explain the greenhouse effect with evidence

items.subject: weather
items.title: What is the weather today?
items.summary: Look out of the window. Sunny, cloudy, rainy or windy? Draw it!
steps: 🪟 Look out of the window.
☀️ Sun? ☁️ Clouds? 🌧️ Rain? 💨 Wind?
🖍️ Draw today's weather.
👕 What should you wear today?
📅 Do it again tomorrow. Is it the same?

items.subject: nature survey
items.title: Doorstep nature spotting
items.summary: How many living things can you spot from your doorstep or window? Look, do not touch.
steps: 👀 Look for a bird, a bug, a leaf and a flower.
✋ Look with your eyes, not your hands.
🔢 Count how many you see.
🖍️ Draw your favourite one.
😊 Tell someone what you found.

safety.notes: Stay on the doorstep, balcony or by a window. An adult is nearby outdoors. Do not touch bugs or pick unknown plants.

advanced.description: Find names in a picture guide.

substitutions.use: a drop of water on clear plastic, or a phone camera zoom

items.subject: recycling
items.title: Sorting rubbish game
items.summary: Paper, plastic, metal or food? Help sort the rubbish into the right box.
steps: 📦 Set out boxes: paper, plastic, metal, food scraps, rubbish.
🧼 Only sort clean, dry items an adult gives you.
🤔 Pick one item. What is it made of?
📥 Put it in the right box.
🔁 Check your local rules: what does your area collect?

safety.notes: Adults handle glass, cans with sharp edges and dirty items. Wash hands afterwards.

better.description: Label boxes with colours and pictures.

advanced.description: Set up a permanent recycling corner.

substitutions.use: cardboard boxes or bags labelled with drawings

items.subject: water cycle
items.title: Water cycle in a bag
items.summary: Make a tiny water cycle and watch clouds and rain happen on a window.
steps: ✏️ Draw a sun, a cloud and waves on a clear zip bag.
💧 Add a little water with a drop of food colouring.
🔒 Seal it tight and tape it to a sunny window.
👀 Check after a few hours: water drops form at the top (condensation).
🌧️ They run down like rain (precipitation).
🗣️ Explain: sun warms water, it evaporates, cools, condenses and falls.

safety.notes: Tape the bag well. No hot water needed.

advanced.description: Bowl with warm water, cling film and ice on top: faster rain.

substitutions.use: a clear plastic bottle with the lid on, or a jar with a lid

check.question: When water vapour cools and turns to drops, it is called...
check.explain: Condensation makes clouds and the drops in your bag.

items.subject: energy saving
items.title: Energy detective
items.summary: Hunt around your home for energy being wasted. Lights on in empty rooms? Doors open?
steps: 🔦 Walk round with an adult.
💡 Count lights on in empty rooms.
🚪 Check: are outside doors and windows closed when heating or cooling is on?
📺 Spot devices left on standby (look, do not touch plugs).
📝 Make a list and share three ideas to save energy.
items.adultNote: Children look and report; adults switch off plugs.

items.subject: composting
items.title: Start a compost bin
items.summary: Food scraps and leaves can turn into rich soil food. Start a small compost bin.
steps: 🪣 Find a bin or box with a lid and some holes for air (an adult makes the holes).
🥬 Greens: fruit and vegetable peel, tea leaves, grass.
🍂 Browns: dry leaves, torn cardboard, paper.
⚖️ Layer about 1 part greens to 2 parts browns.
🚫 No meat, fish, dairy, oil or pet waste.
🔄 Stir every week and keep it damp like a squeezed sponge.
🧼 Wear gloves and wash hands after.
🌱 In a few months, use the dark crumbly compost on plants.

safety.notes: Wear gloves, wash hands, and do not put your face close when opening the bin. Adults make any holes.

basic.description: A small bucket with a lid.

advanced.description: A worm bin to compost faster.

substitutions.use: a lidded bucket on a balcony, or a community compost scheme

items.subject: ecosystems
items.title: Who eats whom? Food webs
items.summary: Every living thing is linked. Plants, plant-eaters and meat-eaters make a food web.
steps: 🌿 Producers: plants make food from sunlight.
🐛 Consumers: animals eat plants or other animals.
🍄 Decomposers: fungi and worms break down dead things into soil.
✏️ Draw a web: grass, rabbit, fox, worm, mushroom, bird.
❓ What happens if one animal disappears? Follow the arrows.

check.question: What do decomposers do?
check.explain: They recycle nutrients back into the soil.

items.subject: weather
items.title: Make a rain gauge and weather diary
items.summary: Measure how much rain falls each day for two weeks, and draw a graph.
steps: 🫙 Use a straight-sided jar.
📏 Stick a ruler or a paper strip marked in millimetres to the side.
🌳 Put it outside in an open place, away from trees and roofs.
⏰ Read it at the same time each day, write it down, then empty it.
📈 After 14 days, draw a bar chart. Which day was wettest?
🌡️ Add temperature and cloud type if you can.

safety.notes: Place it somewhere safe to reach. Use a plastic container if glass may break.

basic.description: A jar with a paper scale.

advanced.description: Compare with a weather station or national weather service data.

substitutions.use: mark centimetres on tape using any ruler from school

items.subject: climate science
items.title: Weather and climate: what is the difference?
items.summary: Weather is today. Climate is the usual weather over many years. Scientists study both.
steps: ☀️ Weather changes every day.
📅 Climate is the average of weather over 30 years or more.
🌍 The Earth is wrapped in air that keeps it warm, like a blanket.
🏭 Burning coal, oil and gas adds more gases to the blanket, so the Earth is slowly warming.
💪 People all over the world are working on solutions: clean energy, planting trees, saving energy.
🌱 You can help too, in small ways, every day.
items.adultNote: Keep the tone hopeful. If a child feels worried, focus on solutions and what people are doing.

items.subject: climate science
items.title: The greenhouse effect and the evidence
items.summary: How greenhouse gases trap heat, and how scientists know the climate is changing.
steps: ☀️ Sunlight reaches the Earth and warms the surface.
🔥 The Earth gives off heat (infrared). Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour absorb some and send it back down.
🧪 Without any greenhouse effect, the Earth would be about -18 °C on average instead of about 15 °C.
📈 Since about 1850, carbon dioxide has risen from about 280 to over 420 parts per million, mainly from burning fossil fuels.
🌡️ Global average temperature is now about 1.1 to 1.3 °C warmer than in the late 1800s.
📚 Evidence: thermometer records, satellites, shrinking glaciers, rising sea level and ice cores.
🔎 Read a page from NASA or the WMO and summarise one graph.

sources.title: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change reports

check.question: Which gas has increased most from burning fossil fuels?
check.explain: Carbon dioxide has risen from about 280 to over 420 parts per million.

items.subject: nature survey
items.title: Square-metre nature survey
items.summary: Mark out a square and count every plant and creature inside. Scientists call this a quadrat survey.
steps: 📏 Mark a 1 m x 1 m square with string and four sticks in a park, verge or yard (ask permission).
🌿 Count each kind of plant and estimate how much of the square it covers (%).
🐜 Count insects and other creatures. Look, do not harm.
📝 Record date, time, weather and place.
🔁 Repeat in a different spot (sunny vs shady) and compare.
📊 Make a chart. Which spot had more variety, and why?
🌍 Share results with a citizen science project if one exists near you.

safety.notes: Go with a friend or tell an adult where you are. Wear gloves, avoid roads, wash hands after.

advanced.description: Photograph and log findings to a citizen science database.

substitutions.use: four sticks and string, or a hula hoop
a pavement crack, a window box or a school yard

items.subject: energy saving
items.title: Calculate a carbon footprint
items.summary: Turn energy use into carbon numbers and find the biggest savings.
steps: 🔌 Electricity: kWh used x the carbon factor for your country (example: 0.4 kg CO2 per kWh).
🧮 Example: 250 kWh a month x 0.4 = 100 kg CO2.
🚗 Travel: car km x about 0.17 kg CO2 per km for an average petrol car.
🧮 Example: 20 km a day x 5 days = 100 km x 0.17 = 17 kg CO2 a week.
🚲 Swap 2 car trips for cycling or walking and calculate the saving.
📝 Write a family action plan with three realistic ideas.
items.adultNote: Carbon factors differ by country and year; the numbers here are illustrative.

items.subject: water saving
items.title: Home water audit
items.summary: Measure how much water your household uses and design a plan to save it.
steps: ⏱️ Time how long it takes a shower to fill a 10-litre bucket. Example: 1 minute = 10 litres per minute.
🧮 An 8-minute shower = 80 litres. 4 people x 80 = 320 litres a day.
🚰 Check for dripping taps and running toilets (put a drop of food colouring in the cistern; if colour appears in the bowl without flushing, it leaks).
📖 Read the water meter if you have one, morning and evening.
💡 Calculate savings from a 4-minute shower.
📝 Present a plan to your family.

safety.notes: Use cool or warm water only. Ask an adult before touching meters or cisterns.

advanced.description: Compare before and after fitting a water-saving head.

substitutions.use: any container: measure its volume by filling with a known-size bottle

items.subject: climate science
items.title: Climate solutions: mitigation and adaptation
items.summary: Explore how the world reduces emissions and adapts to change, and weigh up evidence for each solution.
steps: ⚡ Mitigation: cutting emissions with wind, solar, efficient buildings, public transport and protecting forests.
🛡️ Adaptation: flood defences, drought-resistant crops, early-warning systems, shade and cooling in cities.
📊 Compare two solutions: cost, speed, who benefits, and any downsides.
📚 Use reports from the IPCC or UNEP as sources and note the evidence they give.
🗣️ Present a fair, evidence-based summary to your family or class.
🌱 Choose one action you can take locally.

sources.title: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change reports

items.subject: saving water
items.title: Turn off the tap
items.summary: Water is precious. Turn off the tap when you are not using it!
steps: 💧 Wet your toothbrush or your hands.
🚰 Turn the tap off.
🪥 Brush your teeth or soap your hands.
🚰 Turn the tap on to rinse, then off again.
🌍 Well done, water saver!

safety.notes: Use the cold tap only. Use a sturdy step if needed, with an adult nearby. Wipe up splashes.

basic.description: Turn the tap off while brushing.

better.description: Use a cup of water to rinse your mouth instead of running water.

advanced.description: A water saver chart by the sink for a week.

substitutions.use: a jug or bucket of water: pour only what you need
draw a drop on paper each day you remember

check.question: Brushing teeth. The tap should be...
check.explain: Yes! Turn it off and save water.

check.question: Who needs water?
check.explain: Yes! Every living thing needs water.

items.adultNote: Do it together at the same times every day. If your water comes from a well, tank or tap outside, show how to pour only what is needed.

items.subject: plants
items.title: Water a plant
items.summary: Plants are alive. They need water to grow. You can help!
steps: 👆 Touch the soil. Is it dry?
🥤 Fill a small cup with water.
💧 Pour it slowly onto the soil, not the leaves.
👀 Look at the leaves. Are they green and happy?
📅 Check again tomorrow.

hazards: some house plants are harmful if eaten
safety.notes: Choose a plant an adult knows is safe. Never eat leaves or soil. Wipe spills and wash hands afterwards.

basic.description: Water one plant with a cup.

materials: a plastic bottle with small holes in the lid

advanced.description: Grow your own plant from a seed and look after it.

substitutions.use: a cup, a spoon or a bottle with holes in the lid
a plant outside, a bean in a cup, or a carrot top in a saucer of water

check.question: A plant needs...
check.explain: Yes! Plants need water, light and soil.

check.question: Pour the water on the...
check.explain: Yes! The roots drink from the soil.

items.adultNote: Give a small cup so the plant is not drowned. Let the child feel the soil first: wet means wait. Some house plants are toxic, so choose a safe one.

items.subject: recycling
items.title: Rubbish to seed tray
items.summary: Give rubbish a second life! Turn an old box or carton into a tray for growing seeds.
steps: Find a clean empty carton, egg box or tin.
Ask an adult to poke small holes in the bottom for water to drain.
Fill it with soil.
Push in a few seeds from the kitchen, like coriander, mustard or beans.
Water a little and put it in a bright spot.
Count: how many things did you reuse this week instead of throwing away?

safety.notes: An adult makes the holes and checks tins for sharp edges. Wash hands after touching soil.

basic.description: One reused tray with a few seeds.

better.description: Make three trays and label them with seed names and dates.

advanced.description: Make a bottle mini-greenhouse and move the seedlings to a pot when they grow.

substitutions.use: Old cup, coconut shell, leaf cup or tin
Damp cotton wool or paper for sprouting seeds

items.adultNote: Talk about reduce, reuse and recycle. Reusing something at home often saves more than recycling it.

items.subject: plants
items.title: Why trees keep us cool
items.summary: Find out if the ground under a tree is cooler than the ground in the sun.
steps: Choose a sunny spot and a spot in the shade of a tree or wall.
Put one hand flat on the ground in the sun for 3 seconds. Is it warm or hot?
Now try the ground in the shade.
Which felt cooler? Draw a sun or a cloud face for each spot.
Look for animals or people resting in the shade.
Talk: why might towns plant more trees?

hazards: Very hot ground or metal can burn
safety.notes: Test with the back of the hand first and lift it at once if it feels hot. Never touch metal or dark roads in strong sun. Wear a hat and drink water.

materials: Two cups of water from the same jug
better.description: Leave one cup in sun and one in shade for 20 minutes, then feel which is warmer.

advanced.description: Measure the temperature in sun and shade at three times of day and make a chart.

substitutions.use: The shadow of a wall, building or umbrella
Two cups of water and your fingers to compare

check.question: Where is the ground usually cooler on a sunny day?
check.explain: Leaves block sunlight, so the ground underneath stays cooler.

items.adultNote: Best done in the morning or late afternoon in hot places. Make sure the child never touches very hot surfaces.
